question: Find NPT's audited consolidated statements for the year ended 2023-06-30, or FY2024 statements with 2023 comparatives (not in the nptrust.org sitemap on 2026-11-19; try archived copies of the 2023 and 2024 annual-report pages), and read the net assets held in donor-advised funds at 2023-06-30 to settle whether the filed Schedule D Part I line 4 ($22.84bn, object 202431429349301368) or Part X net assets ($27.92bn) is right
conclusion_affected: FY2023 market total ($256.37bn vs $261.44bn sensitivity), FY2023->24 growth (26.1% vs 23.6%), FY2024 payout on prior-year assets (25.9% vs 25.4%), NPT FY2023 share (8.9% vs 10.7%)
rationale: The return itself is internally inconsistent: Schedule D contributions and grants equal Part VIII/IX in all three years, the DAF value is 101.3% and 100.6% of net assets in FY2022 and FY2024 but 81.8% in FY2023, and both roll-forwards give about $28.2bn. The filing alone cannot show which line is wrong, so the repo keeps the filed value and carries a sensitivity row

question: Screen every DAFRC sponsor-year FY2021-2024 for the NPT pattern: a filed Schedule D Part I line 4 that breaks from the sponsor's own ratio to Part X net assets by more than 10 points against both neighbouring years while contributions and grants stay consistent. List breaks above $250m and test each with a net-asset roll-forward
conclusion_affected: Corrected market totals FY2021-2024 and the growth series
rationale: The R1-R4 rules only replace imputed values, so a filed value that is a keying or definition error passes through unchanged. NPT FY2023 is a $5.08bn example at the #3 sponsor; nobody has screened the rest of the panel the same way

question: UCLA Foundation (EIN 952250801) FY2024: the only FY Jun-2024 Form 990 (object 202521349349311822) reports Schedule D Part I line 3 grants as -$120,260,861, so the repo keeps DAFRC's imputed $169.9m. conclusion_affected: FY2024 corrected grants total ($66.44bn) and the only remaining imputed top-50 metric
rationale: This is the one top-50 FY2024 metric still imputed after round 2. A negative grants figure is a filer error; its absolute value ($120.3m) would cut FY2024 grants by $49.7m if it were adopted
